title: v1/chat.completions: deterministic stop_mode, toolcall preflight handshake, and compact framed-json response
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add `stop_mode` param with deterministic semantics; introduce optional `response_format=framed_json` for compact, line-delimited structured streaming; add toolcall preflight handshake to stabilize function-call streaming boundaries. Backcompat: old defaults preserve prior behavior. SDKs will receive companion adapters.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer reported two classes of intermittent issues: (1) ambiguous stop behavior when multi-token stop sequences overlap role/context boundaries, producing off-by-one tokens in streaming and incorrect logprobs attribution, and (2) streaming tool/function-call boundaries that could split function call JSON across frames causing downstream parsers to fail in edge loads. Additionally, teams wanted a compact, streaming-friendly structured output mode for low-latency consumers.

Summary of changes (single string): This PR introduces three coordinated features: (1) `stop_mode` on the v1/chat endpoint to make stop semantics explicit and deterministic, with three allowed values: `legacy` (current behavior), `exclusive` (stop tokens excluded from returned text), and `deterministic` (choose an unambiguous earliest-match rule with tie-breaks by token index). (2) A toolcall preflight handshake that emits a short, single-frame "toolcall-start" envelope when the model intends to call a function; the runtime reserves a function invocation slot and includes a stable `call_id` to avoid boundary-split parsing during stream fragmentation. (3) `response_format=framed_json`, an opt-in compact mode that returns newline-delimited JSON frames with minimal metadata per frame (role/token/logprob annotations optional) to reduce parsing overhead and improve downstream resilience.

Why these choices: Deterministic stop semantics address observed off-by-one regressions under high-concurrency continuous-batching; introducing an explicit preflight envelope removes the need for heuristic reassembly in downstream consumers and lets us provide strong forward/backward compatibility guarantees. The framed JSON mode is intended for low-latency pipelines (edge devices, thin clients) that prefer line-delimited parsing over chunked text reassembly.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/stream/coordinator.go: add preflight envelope generation and call_id lifecycle management.
- api/v1/chat_handler.go: parse new `stop_mode` and `response_format` params, wire into streaming pipeline.
- model/stopdetector.go: implement deterministic stop matcher and a compatibility wrapper for `legacy` mode.
- streaming/encoder/framed_json_encoder.go: new encoder for framed_json mode with unit tests.
- sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py: parameter translation layer updated; backwards-compatible defaults.
- tests/e2e/chat_stream_toolcall_test.go: new test harness that simulates frame splits and verifies call_id handshake correctness.
- docs/openai_compat.md: describe new params, migration guidance, and example payloads.

Commits summary:
- feat: add stop_mode param and deterministic matcher (model/stopdetector.go, api layer)
- feat: implement toolcall preflight handshake and call_id lifecycle (runtime/stream)
- feat: add framed_json streaming encoder and decoder (streaming/encoder)
- fix: align logprob attribution to deterministic stop cut points
- test: e2e harness for frame-split toolcall behavior
- docs: openai_compat.md additions and examples

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Default behavior remains `stop_mode=legacy` to preserve existing customers.
- Customers who need strict semantics should set `stop_mode=deterministic`. This setting may change token boundaries; recommend validating against existing prompt test suites.
- `response_format=framed_json` is opt-in. Backcompat: clients expecting chunked text will not be affected unless they opt in.
- SDKs: Python/TS adapters include high-level flag `response_format='framed_json'` and helper parsers. We will coordinate releases of the SDK packages in the next minor release window.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: deterministic stop matcher and contrasted cases for overlapping stops.
- Integration: e2e harness simulates fragmentation and concurrent streaming to verify no parse failures and stable call_id mapping.
- Bench: small perf microbench comparing framed_json vs legacy chunked mode (framed_json shows ~4% CPU reduction in simple parser workloads).
- CI: Initial CI run had a flaky streaming encoder test; rerun after adding a short jitter in the test harness to stabilize timing. All checks passed on rerun: unit, integration, lint, e2e, and bench gating.

Review conversation snapshot (condensed):
- Marco Li: "Nice separation of concerns between preflight and payload. Two asks: add a TTL for call_id reservations and ensure we have metrics for reservation leaks."
- Aisha (author): "Added reservation TTL (30s default) and a `stream.call_id_reservations` metric. See runtime/stream/metrics.go change."
- Renee Thompson: "Can we avoid exposing call_id to hosted logs by default?"
- Aisha: "By default call_id is redacted in structured logs for hosted tier; full call_id emitted only for dedicated/private with consent flag. Documented in privacy section."
- Omar Haddad: "Edge case: what happens when the model emits toolcall but the backend is throttled? Ensure we surface a clear fallback (continue as text)."
- Aisha: "Added fallback policy: if reservation fails under throttle we emit `toolcall-fallback` envelope and continue with text fallback; documented and covered by e2e test."
